title: Welcome slate and variant step frames for Quickstart landing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and deliver a cohesive set of Quickstart landing assets centered on a new ‘welcome slate’ concept plus a set of variant step frames that map to user personas and common onboarding paths. This ticket covers: (1) hero/welcome slate compositions (three responsive variants), (2) step frame templates for 1, 3, and 5-step flows including conditional states, (3) screenshot capture specs and automation notes for engineering handoff, (4) accessibility and localization checks, and (5) final assets exported and uploaded to the design asset bucket and documentation pages. Aim: reduce cognitive friction for new users, provide engineering with unambiguous visual tokens for runtime screenshot generation, and ensure visuals are resilient across product changes for upcoming release.
acceptance_criteria: Three approved welcome-slate variants (compact / standard / immersive) with responsive compositions for desktop/tablet/mobile
Step frame templates for 1, 3, and 5-step flows, each with primary, secondary, and error states
Screenshot spec doc (resolution, crop, overlay rules) delivered and linked in the PRD
Figma file updated with components and tokens; handoff tokens include spacing, color variants, and motion durations
Accessibility checklist completed (contrast ratios, semantic alt text, keyboard focus states), and localization pass notes added
Assets exported to /design-assets/quickstart/2026-refresh and QA-reviewed by PM and Eng
deliverables: Figma: Welcome slate master + component variants
Figma: Step frame component kit (1/3/5-step) with conditional overlays
Design spec doc: screenshot-capture-spec.md (resolution, UI toggles, localization rules)
PNG / SVG exports at required sizes and color profiles
Handoff checklist and example screenshot automation config snippets
design_decisions: Adopt a centered ‘slate’ card for initial hero to allow flexible screenshot window overlays
Prioritize a compact variant as default for use in product docs and embedded widgets
Use single accent token for CTA across variants to simplify runtime color replacement via CSS variables
Prefer subtle motion (150ms) for micro transitions to match global motion tokens and keep perceived latency low
